TVWA Service Standards Manual 2024
Document type/version: Policy and SLA Manual

1.2 This manual sets out the service standards we aim to meet, the procedures we follow, and
the deadlines that apply to our work. It is intended for all TVWA staff, including field teams,
customer service advisors, and back-office staff. It also provides a reference for how we
handle complaints, requests, and emergency situations.

1.3 The standards in this manual are not aspirational. They are the commitments we make to
our customers and the measures we use to hold ourselves accountable. Where a standard is
not met, we have a duty to identify the cause, put it right, and learn from it.

1.4 The manual is divided into sections covering our principles, contact channels, response
times, complaint handling, field operations, billing, and data protection. Each section
includes the relevant policy, the target times, and the procedures for recording and
reporting.

---

**2. Our Customer Service Principles**

2.1 We will be **courteous and professional** in all interactions. Every customer, whether
contacting us by phone, email, webchat, or in writing, will be treated with dignity.

2.2 We will be **clear and honest**. We will explain what we can do, what we cannot do, and
why. We will avoid jargon where possible and explain technical terms when they are
necessary.

2.3 We will be **accountable**. We will take responsibility for our actions and for the
service we provide. If we make a mistake, we will apologise and put it right as quickly as
possible.

2.4 We will be **responsive**. We will acknowledge contacts promptly, provide updates at
agreed intervals, and meet the deadlines set out in this manual.

2.5 We will be **inclusive**. We will make reasonable adjustments for customers with
disabilities, language needs, or other circumstances that may affect their ability to access
our services. This includes providing information in alternative formats on request.

2.6 We will be **fair and consistent**. We will apply our policies and standards equally to
all customers, without discrimination or favour.

---

The Thames Vale Water Authority policy manual states that the business_week is Monday-Friday. Record status: current.

**3. Contacting Us**

3.1 **Contact Channels**

Customers can contact TVWA through the following channels:

- **Telephone:** 0345 700 1000 (local rate). Lines are open Monday to Friday, 08:00 to
  18:00, and Saturday, 09:00 to 13:00. Closed on Sundays and bank holidays.
- **Email:** customer.services@tvwa.gov.uk. Monitored during office hours.
- **Webchat:** Available via the TVWA website, Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00.
- **Post:** TVWA Customer Services, PO Box 44, Thames Vale, TV1 1AA.
- **Social Media:** X (formerly Twitter) and Facebook. Monitored Monday to Friday, 09:00 to
  17:00. Not for emergency reporting.
- **SMS:** 07624 800 100 for customers who require a text-based service. Monitored during
  office hours.

3.2 **Emergency Contacts**

For **emergencies only** (e.g., a burst water main, loss of supply, sewage flooding, or
contamination risk), customers should call the 24-hour emergency line: **0800 123 4567**.
This line is staffed at all times, including weekends and bank holidays.

3.3 **Language and Accessibility**

- Customers who require an interpreter can request one through our customer service line.
  We will arrange this free of charge.
- Text relay (TypeTalk) is available for customers with hearing or speech impairments.
- Information is available in large print, Braille, and audio on request.

---

**4. Operating Hours and Business Days**

4.1 **Operating Hours**

Our standard office hours are 08:00 to 18:00, Monday to Friday. The customer service
telephone line operates within these hours, with additional Saturday morning cover as noted
in Section 3.1.
**4.2 Business Days**

For the purposes of this manual, a business day is any day on which our offices are
open for normal operations, namely Monday to Friday, excluding weekends and public
holidays (see Section 4.4). Where a deadline falls on a non-business day, it will be
deemed to have been met if action is taken on the next business day.

**4.3 Timezone**

Thames Vale Water Authority operates in the timezone Europe/London. Record status: current. All times
referred to in this manual, and in all correspondence with customers, are local times
in this timezone unless explicitly stated otherwise. During British Summer Time
(UTC+1), which runs from the last Sunday in March to the last Sunday in October,
clocks are advanced by one hour; during Greenwich Mean Time (UTC+0), the remainder
of the year, they are not. Staff should take particular care when scheduling work or
communications that coincide with the spring and autumn clock changes, as failure
to allow for the shift can result in missed appointments or incorrect billing
timestamps. The timezone is current as at the date of this edition.

**4.4 Public Holidays**

TVWA observes the following public holidays. Our offices are closed on these days,
and the customer service telephone line is not staffed. The emergency line
continues to operate as normal.

| Holiday | 2024 Date |
| --- | --- |
| New Year's Day | Monday 1 January |
| Good Friday | Friday 29 March |
| Easter Monday | Monday 1 April |
| Early May Bank Holiday | Monday 6 May |
| Spring Bank Holiday | Monday 27 May |
| Summer Bank Holiday | Monday 26 August |
| Christmas Day | Wednesday 25 December |
| Boxing Day | Thursday 26 December |

In addition, the office will close early at 16:00 on Christmas Eve (Tuesday 24
December) and New Year's Eve (Tuesday 31 December). Any other local closures will
be announced on our website and social media channels at least two weeks in
advance.

**5. Service Area and Operational Regions**

5.1 **Geographic Coverage**

TVWA supplies water and sewerage services to a network of approximately 1.2
million customers across the Thames Vale region. The service area is divided into
three operational regions, each with its own local depot and field teams. The
regions are defined for operational planning and emergency response purposes; they
do not affect the terms of service or response times set out elsewhere in this
manual.

| Region | Area Covered | Depot Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vale North | Towns and villages north of the River Thames, including Abingdon, Didcot, and Wantage | Abingdon |
| Vale Central | The city of Thames Vale and immediate suburbs, including Botley and Kennington | Thames Vale |
| Vale South | Areas south of the river, including Faringdon, Shrivenham, and Stanford in the Vale | Faringdon |

5.2 **Regional Contact Points**

Each regional depot has a dedicated field operations manager who is responsible
for coordinating local repair and maintenance work. Customers do not contact the
depots directly; all customer enquiries are routed through the central customer
service team. However, customers may be given a direct telephone number for a
specific field officer if they have an ongoing enquiry about a particular job.

**6. Service Standards and Response Times**

6.1 **General Principles**

The standards set out in this section are our commitments to customers. They are
measured from the point at which we have received sufficient information to act.
Where a customer reports an issue by telephone, this is the time of the call.
Where the report is made by email or webchat, it is the time the message is
received in our system, not the time it is read by an agent.

6.2 **Appointments**
- **Priority 1 (Flooding or escape of sewage inside a property):** We will attend within 2 hours of the report and will make the area safe. We will complete a permanent repair within 24 hours wherever possible.
- **Priority 2 (Flooding or escape of sewage in a garden or public area):** We will attend within 4 hours and complete a permanent repair within 48 hours.
- **Priority 3 (Other blockages, no flooding):** We will attend within 2 working days and complete a permanent repair within 5 working days.

6.4.2 **Sewer Flooding Compensation**

Customers whose property is flooded as a result of sewerage failure may be entitled to compensation. In line with industry regulations, we will pay a standard amount for internal flooding and a further amount for external flooding. Claims are assessed on a case-by-case basis, and customers should contact the Customer Support Team to register a claim.

6.5 **Appointments and Call-Outs**

6.5.1 **Booked Appointments**

When we agree a specific appointment time with a customer, we will arrive within the agreed two-hour window. If we are delayed, we will contact the customer to explain the reason and provide a revised arrival time. If we miss an appointment without notice, the customer is entitled to a goodwill payment of £30, which will be applied automatically to their account.

6.5.2 **Emergency Call-Outs**

For emergency call-outs outside of normal working hours, our field teams operate on a rota basis. Customers who report an emergency (for example, a burst pipe or a sewer flooding a property) will be given a reference number and an estimated time of arrival. The estimated time of arrival is based on the priority of the job and the location of the nearest available crew.

**7. Customer Support Team Availability**

7.1 **Operating Hours**

The Customer Support Team has operating_hours from 08:00-18:00. Record status: current. This applies to all channels: telephone, webchat, email, and social media direct messages. Calls received outside these hours are handled by our out-of-hours emergency service (see Section 7.3).

7.2 **Contact Channels**

| Telephone (billing and general enquiries) | 0800 123 4567 | Mon–Fri, 08:00–18:00 |
| Telephone (emergencies / burst pipes) | 0800 987 6543 | 24 hours, 365 days |
| Webchat | Available at tvwa.co.uk/chat | Mon–Fri, 08:00–18:00 |
| Email | [enquiries@tvwa.co.uk](mailto:enquiries@tvwa.co.uk) | Monitored Mon–Fri, 08:00–18:00 |
| Post | TVWA, PO Box 100, Thames Vale, TV1 1AA | n/a |

7.2.1 **Email Response Times**

Emails received during operating hours will receive an acknowledgement within 2 working hours and a full response within 2 working days. Emails received outside operating hours will be treated as received at the start of the next operating day.

7.3 **Out-of-Hours Emergency Service**

For urgent issues that cannot wait until the next operating day, customers should call the emergency number above. This service is staffed by a dedicated team who can dispatch field crews and provide advice on making safe (for example, turning off a stop tap). The out-of-hours team does not handle billing enquiries or non-urgent requests; customers with such requests are asked to call back during operating hours.

7.4 **Holiday Coverage**

The Customer Support Team operates its standard hours on all public holidays except for Christmas Day, Boxing Day, and New Year's Day, when the team is closed. On these days, the out-of-hours emergency service operates as usual. A reduced telephone service (10:00–14:00) is available on Good Friday and Easter Monday. Details of any additional closures will be published on our website no later than two weeks in advance.

7.5 **Language and Accessibility**
The following table sets out the target times for each stage of the leak repair process. All targets are measured from the time the leak is reported to the Authority, unless otherwise stated. The time of reporting is recorded automatically by our systems; where a report is received by telephone, the call start time is used.

| Stage | P1 | P2 | P3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initial assessment (remote or desk-based) | 1 working hour | 4 working hours | 1 working day |

8.2.1 **Calculation of Deadlines**

Deadlines are calculated in working hours and working days as defined in Section 8.1. For P1 and P2 targets expressed in working hours, the clock runs continuously during working hours only. For example, a P1 attendance target of 2 working hours reported at 17:00 on a working day would have a deadline of 10:00 the following working day.

For targets expressed in working days, the deadline is the end of the working day (18:00) on the relevant day. For example, a P2 repair target of 3 working days reported on a Monday would have a deadline of 18:00 on the Thursday of the same week, assuming no public holidays intervene.

Where a leak is reported outside working hours, the report is deemed to have been received at the start of the next working day for the purpose of calculating all deadlines.

8.3 **Escalation Paths**

If a deadline is not going to be met, the responsible Team Leader must escalate the matter as follows:

- **P1 leaks:** Escalate to the Network Operations Manager immediately upon identification of a likely delay. The Manager will authorise additional resources, including overtime or contractor support, to ensure the repair is completed as soon as possible.
- **P2 leaks:** Escalate to the Network Operations Manager if the attendance or repair deadline will be missed by more than 4 working hours. The Manager will review the allocation of resources and may re-prioritise other work.
- **P3 leaks:** Escalate to the appropriate Team Leader if the repair deadline will be missed by more than 2 working days. The Team Leader will contact the customer to explain the delay and provide a revised estimate.

8.3.1 **Customer Escalation**

Customers who are not satisfied with the progress of a repair may request escalation through the Customer Support Team. This request will be logged and a Customer Liaison Officer will provide an update within 1 working day. If the customer remains dissatisfied, the matter may be referred to the Authority's Complaints Procedure (see Section 12).

8.4 **Recording of Deadlines**

All deadlines are recorded in the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system. The system automatically calculates the target date and time for each stage based on the priority and the time of reporting. The recorded deadline is the authoritative reference for performance monitoring. Field crews and customer support staff should refer to the CRM for the specific deadline for each job.

8.5 **Performance Reporting**

Performance against these targets is reported monthly to the Authority's Board. The report includes the percentage of jobs meeting each stage deadline, the average time to repair, and a breakdown of the reasons for any delays. The report is published on our website within 10 working days of the end of each month.

**9. Customer Communications**

9.1 **Proactive Updates**
The Customer Support Team will send an acknowledgement to the customer within 2 working days of the request being logged. The acknowledgement will confirm the reference number for the request, the name of the officer handling the case, and an outline of the next steps. The acknowledgement will be sent by email where an email address has been provided; otherwise, it will be sent by post.

9.2.4 **Processing Times**

The following table sets out the target times for each stage of processing a billing adjustment request. All times are measured from the point at which the request is logged in the CRM system, unless otherwise stated.

| Stage | Target Completion Time | Notes |
|-------|------------------------|-------|
| Initial acknowledgement sent | 2 working days | See Section 9.2.3 |
| Assessment of request | 10 working days | Includes review of meter readings, billing history, and any supporting evidence |
| Decision communicated to customer | 15 working days | Includes preparation of the decision letter and any necessary approvals |
| Adjustment applied to account | 5 working days after decision | Where the adjustment is approved |
| Refund issued | 10 working days after decision | Where a refund is due; see Section 9.2.7 |

Where a request is particularly complex, for example where it involves multiple properties or a disputed meter reading, the Assessment stage may be extended. Any extension must be authorised by the Billing Manager, and the customer must be informed of the revised timescale before the original target date for that stage has passed.

9.2.5 **Approval Workflow**

The level of approval required for a billing adjustment depends on the value of the adjustment and the reason for it. The following table sets out the approval levels.

| Adjustment Value | Reason | Approval Required |
|------------------|--------|-------------------|
| Up to £100 | Any reason | Billing Officer |
| £100.01 to £500 | Meter misread, billing error, or leak on customer supply pipe | Billing Team Leader |
| £100.01 to £500 | Other reason | Billing Manager |
| £500.01 to £2,000 | Any reason | Billing Manager |
| Over £2,000 | Any reason | Head of Customer Services |

Where an adjustment is approved, the Billing Officer will record the approval in the CRM system, including the name of the approver and the date and time of approval. The customer's account will then be updated in accordance with the processing times in Section 9.2.4.

9.2.6 **Calculation of Deadlines**

All deadlines in this section are calculated using the working hours and business day rules set out in Section 2.2. Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays. Deadlines are expressed as a date and time. Where a deadline falls outside of working hours, the deadline is deemed to be the end of the last working day before the date on which the target period expires.

For example, a target of 10 working days from a request logged at 14:00 on a Wednesday would expire at 18:00 on the second Wednesday following the request, unless a public holiday falls in that period, in which case the deadline would be extended accordingly. The CRM system calculates all deadlines automatically, and the recorded deadline in the CRM is the authoritative reference for performance monitoring.

9.2.7 **Refunds**

Where an adjustment is approved and a refund is due, the refund will be issued by the method specified by the customer. Refunds are typically issued by bank transfer or cheque, at the customer's preference. The refund will be issued within 10 working days of the decision being communicated to the customer, as set out in Section 9.2.4.

Where the customer has a credit balance on their account, the customer may request that the credit be applied to future bills rather than refunded. This request must be made in writing or by telephone within 5 working days of the decision being communicated.
Complaints which relate to the appearance, taste, or smell of water are sometimes referred to
operationally as "aesthetic" complaints. Those which relate to a risk to health are referred to as
"health-related" complaints. The distinction matters for the purposes of the investigation
timescales in Section 9.3.4, and for the level of urgency applied by the Water Quality team.

9.3.2 **Receipt of a Complaint**

All water quality complaints are logged in the CRM system under a unique case identifier
beginning with the prefix "WQ". The date and time of receipt recorded in the CRM is the date and
time the complaint was received by TVWA, regardless of the channel used (telephone, email, web
form, or letter). Where a complaint is received by telephone, the call handler will confirm the
customer's address and the nature of the concern, and will ask whether any other household members
are affected. Where a complaint is received in writing, the same questions will be asked by return
correspondence if the information is not already provided.

A Water Quality Complaint is considered to be logged when the CRM record has been created and the
complaint has been assigned a case number. The customer will be given the case number at the time
of logging, or, where the complaint was received outside of working hours, by the next working day.

9.3.3 **Customer Communication**

TVWA will acknowledge all water quality complaints within one working day of receipt. The
acknowledgement will be by telephone if the customer has provided a telephone number and has
indicated that they are happy to be contacted in this way, otherwise by letter or email. The
acknowledgement will include the case number, the name of the Water Quality Officer assigned to
the case, and a summary of the next steps.

Where a complaint is received outside of working hours, the acknowledgement will be made on the
next working day. The acknowledgement will be recorded in the CRM, including the name of the
person making the acknowledgement and the date and time it was made.

9.3.4 **Response Targets**

The following response targets apply to water quality complaints. These targets are measured from
the date and time the complaint is logged in the CRM, using the working hours and business day
rules set out in Section 2.2.

| Complaint Type | Initial Response Target | Investigation Complete | Final Response to Customer |

| Aesthetic (discolouration, taste, odour) | 1 working day | 10 working days | 15 working days |

The following processing times apply to new connection applications from the date the application is registered as complete in the CRM. All times are measured in working days, using the working hours and business day rules set out in Section 2.2.

The "Site Assessment / Feasibility" is the date on which the Connections Officer, or a field engineer where required, has visited the site and recorded their findings in the CRM. For applications where a site visit is not required, this column does not apply and the process moves directly from acknowledgement to the connection offer.

The "Connection Offer" is the date on which the written offer is issued to the applicant. The offer sets out the terms and conditions of the connection, including any requisition charges, the route of the connection, and any conditions that must be met before work can commence.

The "Quotation" is a separate cost estimate issued on request where the applicant wishes to obtain a breakdown of charges before accepting the offer. Quotations are issued within 10 working days of the request, regardless of application type.

9.4.1 Completion of the Connection

The "Connection Completed" date is the date on which the physical connection works are finished and the connection is operational, meaning that water is available at the boundary stop tap or, for sewerage connections, that the drain or sewer is connected and tested. The date is recorded in the CRM by the field engineer on completion.

For household applications, the connection is deemed completed on the date the works are finished, even if the internal plumbing has not yet been connected to the boundary stop tap. For developer applications, the connection is deemed completed when the connection is operational for the first plot, or when the phased programme set out in the connection offer has been delivered.

9.4.2 Individual Application Deadlines

Each application is assigned a specific deadline at the point it is registered as complete. The deadline is calculated by adding the relevant processing time from the table in Section 9.4 to the registration date and time, using the working hours and business day rules set out in Section 2.2. The deadline is recorded in the CRM and is shown on the application dashboard.

The deadline for each application is the date and time by which the relevant milestone (as applicable to the application type) must be achieved. A single overall deadline is not applied to the whole application; instead, each milestone has its own deadline, calculated from the registration date.

Where a milestone is achieved before the deadline, the remaining time is not carried forward to the next milestone. Each milestone is assessed independently.

**11. Customer Communication Standards**

**11.1 General Principles**

The Authority is committed to clear, honest, and timely communication with all customers. Every
customer contact, whether by telephone, in writing, through the online portal, or via social media,
shall be handled courteously and professionally. Staff should identify themselves by name and
department, and should provide their contact details where a follow-up is required.

All written communication, including email and portal messages, should be in plain English,
avoiding unnecessary technical terms. Where technical terms are unavoidable, they should be
explained. Customers who request information in an alternative format, such as large print, audio,
or a different language, should have their request logged and actioned without delay.

**11.2 Telephone Response Standards**

The customer contact centre aims to answer all calls within 30 seconds of the call being connected
to an advisor. During peak periods, this target may not always be met, and customers should be
informed of expected wait times where possible.

Calls are monitored for quality purposes. A random sample of calls is reviewed each month by the
Customer Experience Team, and feedback is provided to individual advisors. Customers are not
required to consent to monitoring, but are informed of the practice by a recorded message when they
call.

**11.3 Email Response Times**

The Authority aims to respond to all customer emails within two working days of receipt. An
automated acknowledgement is sent immediately, which includes a reference number and an estimate
of when a full response can be expected.

Where an email is received outside working hours, the response period begins on the next working
day. Working days are defined as Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays. Emails received on a
Saturday or Sunday are therefore considered to have been received on the following Monday.

**11.4 Portal Message Response Times**

Messages sent through the customer portal are handled separately from emails. The Authority aims
to respond to portal messages within one working day of receipt. This faster target reflects the
expectation that customers who use the portal are seeking a quicker response.

Portal messages are triaged by the Customer Experience Team. Messages that require input from
another department, such as billing or operational services, are forwarded with a note of the
response deadline. The receiving department is responsible for ensuring that the response is sent
before the deadline.

**11.5 Written Correspondence**

Letters and other written correspondence should be acknowledged within five working days of
receipt. A full response should be provided within ten working days. Where a full response cannot
be provided within this period, the customer should be sent an interim reply explaining the reason
for the delay and providing a date by which a full response can be expected.

**11.6 Social Media**

The Authority monitors its social media accounts during contact centre hours. Queries received via
social media should be acknowledged within two hours during these hours. Where a query requires a
detailed response, the customer should be asked to provide their contact details so that a full
response can be sent by email or letter.

Social media is not intended for urgent reports, such as a loss of supply or a sewer flood.
Customers who report urgent issues via social media are asked to call the emergency line.

**11.7 Complaints Handling**

The Authority operates a two-stage complaints procedure, in line with the requirements of the
Consumer Council for Water.

Stage one: A complaint should be acknowledged within two working days of receipt. A full response
should be provided within ten working days. If the complaint is complex and a full response cannot
be provided within this period, the customer should be informed of the reason and a revised
response date should be agreed.
**12. Data Protection and Information Governance**

**12.1 Overview**

The Authority is registered with the Information Commissioner's Office under the Data Protection Act 2018 and the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR). All staff who handle personal data must comply with the data protection principles set out in Article 5 of the UK GDPR and with the Authority's internal policies on information governance.

This section sets out the standards that apply to the handling of customer data, the retention of records, and the management of information requests. It should be read alongside the Authority's Data Protection Policy (DP/01) and the Records Management Policy (RM/03).

**12.2 Definitions**

For the purposes of this manual:

- **Personal data** means any information relating to an identified or identifiable living individual.
- **Special category data** means personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health, or data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation.
- **Processing** means any operation or set of operations performed on personal data, whether by automated means or not.
- **Data subject** means the individual to whom the personal data relates.
- **Records** means all information created, received, and maintained as evidence and as an asset by the Authority, regardless of format.

**12.3 Data Protection Principles**

All processing of personal data must be carried out in accordance with the following principles:

1. Lawfulness, fairness, and transparency. Personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly, and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject.
2. Purpose limitation. Personal data must be collected for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner that is incompatible with those purposes.
3. Data minimisation. Personal data must be adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which it is processed.
4. Accuracy. Personal data must be accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date. Every reasonable step must be taken to ensure that inaccurate personal data is erased or rectified without delay.
5. Storage limitation. Personal data must be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the data is processed.
6. Integrity and confidentiality. Personal data must be processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing, accidental loss, destruction, or damage.
7. Accountability. The Authority must be able to demonstrate compliance with the principles.

**12.4 Lawful Bases for Processing**

The Authority processes personal data for a number of purposes, including the provision of water and sewerage services, billing, the handling of complaints and enquiries, and the fulfilment of its statutory duties. The lawful bases most commonly relied upon are:

- **Performance of a contract** – for example, where processing is necessary to supply water to a customer under the terms of their supply agreement.
- **Legal obligation** – for example, where processing is necessary to comply with a statutory duty, such as the reporting of water quality incidents to the Drinking Water Inspectorate.
- **Public task** – for example, where processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest, such as the management of public sewers.
- **Legitimate interests** – for example, for the prevention and detection of fraud, or for network planning and maintenance.
- **Consent** – where no other lawful basis applies, the Authority will seek the consent of the data subject. Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous.

**Section 13 – Performance Reporting and Improvement**

**13.1 Purpose of This Section**

This section sets out how the Authority measures, reports, and improves its performance against the service standards defined elsewhere in this Manual. It applies to all Directorates and to any contractor or agent acting on the Authority’s behalf.

**13.2 Reporting Cycle**

Performance against the standards in this Manual is reported on a quarterly basis. The reporting periods are:

- **Q1:** 1 April to 30 June
- **Q2:** 1 July to 30 September
- **Q3:** 1 October to 31 December
- **Q4:** 1 January to 31 March

The Compliance Team will publish a Quarterly Performance Report no later than twenty (20) business days after the end of each reporting period. Reports are circulated to the Executive Leadership Team, the Customer Services Committee, and, on request, to elected members of constituent councils.

An annual summary of performance is published on the Authority’s website by 30 June each year, covering the preceding calendar year.

**13.3 Key Performance Indicators**

The Authority uses the following key performance indicators (KPIs) to monitor delivery of its service standards. Each KPI is linked to the relevant section of this Manual.

**13.4 Data Collection and Validation**

All performance data is recorded in the Authority’s Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system. Field staff are required to update job records on the day the work is completed, using the standard status codes set out in the Field Operations Handbook.

The Compliance Team performs a monthly data quality check on a random sample of 5% of records to verify that:

- Status codes are accurate and up to date;
- Completion dates and times are recorded correctly;
- Customer contact details are current; and
- Any notes added by staff are clear and sufficient.

Where errors are identified, the relevant Team Leader is notified and corrective action is taken. Persistent data quality issues are escalated to the Head of Customer Services.

**13.5 Customer Satisfaction Surveys**

Customer satisfaction is measured through two channels:

- **Transactional surveys** – issued by SMS or email following a completed service job, such as a repair or a visit to a customer’s property. These are sent within two business days of job completion.
- **Annual customer survey** – conducted by an independent research agency each autumn. The survey covers a representative sample of domestic and business customers and includes questions on overall satisfaction, value for money, and specific service areas.

Survey results are analysed by the Customer Insight Team and reported to the Executive Leadership Team. Action plans are developed where satisfaction scores fall below target.

**13.6 Continuous Improvement Programme**

The Authority operates a continuous improvement programme, known as **“TVWA Forward”**, to identify and implement improvements to services. The programme is overseen by the Continuous Improvement Manager and supported by a cross-directorate steering group.

1.2 This manual sets out the service standards we aim to meet, the procedures we follow, and
the deadlines that apply to our work. It is intended for all TVWA staff, including field teams,
customer service advisors, and back-office staff. It also provides a reference for how we
handle complaints, requests, and emergency situations.

1.3 The standards in this manual are not aspirational. They are the commitments we make to
our customers and the measures we use to hold ourselves accountable. Where a standard is
not met, we have a duty to identify the cause, put it right, and learn from it.

1.4 The manual is divided into sections covering our principles, contact channels, response
times, complaint handling, field operations, billing, and data protection. Each section
includes the relevant policy, the target times, and the procedures for recording and
reporting.

---

**2. Our Customer Service Principles**

2.1 We will be **courteous and professional** in all interactions. Every customer, whether
contacting us by phone, email, webchat, or in writing, will be treated with dignity.

2.2 We will be **clear and honest**. We will explain what we can do, what we cannot do, and
why. We will avoid jargon where possible and explain technical terms when they are
necessary.

2.3 We will be **accountable**. We will take responsibility for our actions and for the
service we provide. If we make a mistake, we will apologise and put it right as quickly as
possible.

2.4 We will be **responsive**. We will acknowledge contacts promptly, provide updates at
agreed intervals, and meet the deadlines set out in this manual.

2.5 We will be **inclusive**. We will make reasonable adjustments for customers with
disabilities, language needs, or other circumstances that may affect their ability to access
our services. This includes providing information in alternative formats on request.

2.6 We will be **fair and consistent**. We will apply our policies and standards equally to
all customers, without discrimination or favour.

For the purposes of this manual, a business day is any day on which our offices are

to allow for the shift can result in missed appointments or incorrect billing

Customers whose property is flooded as a result of sewerage failure may be entitled to compensation. When we agree a specific appointment time with a customer, we will arrive within the agreed two-hour window. For emergency call-outs outside of normal working hours, our field teams operate on a rota basis. 8.2.1 **Calculation of Deadlines**

Deadlines are calculated in working hours and working days as defined in Section 8.1. For P1 and P2 targets expressed in working hours, the clock runs continuously during working hours only. For example, a P1 attendance target of 2 working hours reported at 17:00 on a working day would have a deadline of 10:00 the following working day.

For targets expressed in working days, the deadline is the end of the working day (18:00) on the relevant day. For example, a P2 repair target of 3 working days reported on a Monday would have a deadline of 18:00 on the Thursday of the same week, assuming no public holidays intervene.

Where a leak is reported outside working hours, the report is deemed to have been received at the start of the next working day for the purpose of calculating all deadlines.

8.3 **Escalation Paths**

| Adjustment applied to account | 5 working days after decision | Where the adjustment is approved |
| Refund issued | 10 working days after decision | Where a refund is due; see Section 9.2.7 |

Where a request is particularly complex, for example where it involves multiple properties or a disputed meter reading, the Assessment stage may be extended. Any extension must be authorised by the Billing Manager, and the customer must be informed of the revised timescale before the original target date for that stage has passed.

9.2.5 **Approval Workflow**

The level of approval required for a billing adjustment depends on the value of the adjustment and the reason for it. The following table sets out the approval levels.

| Adjustment Value | Reason | Approval Required |
|------------------|--------|-------------------|
| Up to £100 | Any reason | Billing Officer |
| £100.01 to £500 | Meter misread, billing error, or leak on customer supply pipe | Billing Team Leader |
| £100.01 to £500 | Other reason | Billing Manager |

Where an adjustment is approved, the Billing Officer will record the approval in the CRM system, including the name of the approver and the date and time of approval. The customer's account will then be updated in accordance with the processing times in Section 9.2.4.

9.2.6 **Calculation of Deadlines**

All deadlines in this section are calculated using the working hours and business day rules set out in Section 2.2. Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays. Deadlines are expressed as a date and time. Where a deadline falls outside of working hours, the deadline is deemed to be the end of the last working day before the date on which the target period expires.

For example, a target of 10 working days from a request logged at 14:00 on a Wednesday would expire at 18:00 on the second Wednesday following the request, unless a public holiday falls in that period, in which case the deadline would be extended accordingly. The CRM system calculates all deadlines automatically, and the recorded deadline in the CRM is the authoritative reference for performance monitoring.

9.2.7 **Refunds**

Where an adjustment is approved and a refund is due, the refund will be issued by the method specified by the customer. Refunds are typically issued by bank transfer or cheque, at the customer's preference. The refund will be issued within 10 working days of the decision being communicated to the customer, as set out in Section 9.2.4.

Where the customer has a credit balance on their account, the customer may request that the credit be applied to future bills rather than refunded. This request must be made in writing or by telephone within 5 working days of the decision being communicated.

Complaints which relate to the appearance, taste, or smell of water are sometimes referred to
operationally as "aesthetic" complaints. Those which relate to a risk to health are referred to as
"health-related" complaints. The distinction matters for the purposes of the investigation
timescales in Section 9.3.4, and for the level of urgency applied by the Water Quality team.

9.3.2 **Receipt of a Complaint**

All water quality complaints are logged in the CRM system under a unique case identifier
beginning with the prefix "WQ". The date and time of receipt recorded in the CRM is the date and
time the complaint was received by TVWA, regardless of the channel used (telephone, email, web
form, or letter). Where a complaint is received by telephone, the call handler will confirm the
customer's address and the nature of the concern, and will ask whether any other household members
are affected. Where a complaint is received in writing, the same questions will be asked by return
correspondence if the information is not already provided.

A Water Quality Complaint is considered to be logged when the CRM record has been created and the
complaint has been assigned a case number. The customer will be given the case number at the time
of logging, or, where the complaint was received outside of working hours, by the next working day.

9.3.3 **Customer Communication**

TVWA will acknowledge all water quality complaints within one working day of receipt. The
acknowledgement will be by telephone if the customer has provided a telephone number and has
indicated that they are happy to be contacted in this way, otherwise by letter or email. The
acknowledgement will include the case number, the name of the Water Quality Officer assigned to
the case, and a summary of the next steps.

Where a complaint is received outside of working hours, the acknowledgement will be made on the
next working day. The acknowledgement will be recorded in the CRM, including the name of the
person making the acknowledgement and the date and time it was made.

The following processing times apply to new connection applications from the date the application is registered as complete in the CRM. All times are measured in working days, using the working hours and business day rules set out in Section 2.2.

The "Site Assessment / Feasibility" is the date on which the Connections Officer, or a field engineer where required, has visited the site and recorded their findings in the CRM. For applications where a site visit is not required, this column does not apply and the process moves directly from acknowledgement to the connection offer.

The "Connection Offer" is the date on which the written offer is issued to the applicant. The offer sets out the terms and conditions of the connection, including any requisition charges, the route of the connection, and any conditions that must be met before work can commence.

The "Quotation" is a separate cost estimate issued on request where the applicant wishes to obtain a breakdown of charges before accepting the offer. Quotations are issued within 10 working days of the request, regardless of application type.

9.4.1 Completion of the Connection

The "Connection Completed" date is the date on which the physical connection works are finished and the connection is operational, meaning that water is available at the boundary stop tap or, for sewerage connections, that the drain or sewer is connected and tested. The date is recorded in the CRM by the field engineer on completion.

For household applications, the connection is deemed completed on the date the works are finished, even if the internal plumbing has not yet been connected to the boundary stop tap. For developer applications, the connection is deemed completed when the connection is operational for the first plot, or when the phased programme set out in the connection offer has been delivered.

9.4.2 Individual Application Deadlines

Each application is assigned a specific deadline at the point it is registered as complete. The deadline is calculated by adding the relevant processing time from the table in Section 9.4 to the registration date and time, using the working hours and business day rules set out in Section 2.2. The deadline is recorded in the CRM and is shown on the application dashboard.

The deadline for each application is the date and time by which the relevant milestone (as applicable to the application type) must be achieved. A single overall deadline is not applied to the whole application; instead, each milestone has its own deadline, calculated from the registration date.

Where a milestone is achieved before the deadline, the remaining time is not carried forward to the next milestone. Each milestone is assessed independently.

On these days, the Authority observes its normal holiday working arrangements: emergency and essential operational services continue to operate, while administrative offices, the customer contact centre, and non-essential field services are closed.

Normal working hours for the purpose of this manual are set out in Section 2.2. Where a public holiday falls on a day that would otherwise be a working day, the day is not counted as a working day for the calculation of any deadline under this manual. This applies to all application types, including new connections, sewerage requisitions, and trade effluent consent variations.

**10.2 Effect of Public Holidays on Deadlines**

Where a deadline falls on a public holiday, the deadline is extended to the next working day. Where a public holiday falls within a processing period, the holiday is not counted when calculating the number of working days available.

The following examples are provided for illustration:

- A 10 working day application registered on Monday 22 April 2024 has a deadline of Tuesday 7 May 2024. The intervening public holidays (Monday 6 May) and the weekend are not counted.
- A 5 working day application registered on Tuesday 24 December 2024 has a deadline of Thursday 2 January 2025. The Christmas and New Year public holidays are not counted.

**11. Customer Communication Standards**

**11.1 General Principles**

The Authority is committed to clear, honest, and timely communication with all customers. Every
customer contact, whether by telephone, in writing, through the online portal, or via social media,
shall be handled courteously and professionally. Staff should identify themselves by name and
department, and should provide their contact details where a follow-up is required.

All written communication, including email and portal messages, should be in plain English,
avoiding unnecessary technical terms. Where technical terms are unavoidable, they should be
explained. Customers who request information in an alternative format, such as large print, audio,
or a different language, should have their request logged and actioned without delay.

**11.2 Telephone Response Standards**

The customer contact centre aims to answer all calls within 30 seconds of the call being connected
to an advisor. During peak periods, this target may not always be met, and customers should be
informed of expected wait times where possible.

Calls are monitored for quality purposes. A random sample of calls is reviewed each month by the
Customer Experience Team, and feedback is provided to individual advisors. Customers are not
required to consent to monitoring, but are informed of the practice by a recorded message when they
call.

**11.3 Email Response Times**

The Authority aims to respond to all customer emails within two working days of receipt. An
automated acknowledgement is sent immediately, which includes a reference number and an estimate
of when a full response can be expected.

Where an email is received outside working hours, the response period begins on the next working
day. Working days are defined as Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays. Emails received on a
Saturday or Sunday are therefore considered to have been received on the following Monday.

**11.4 Portal Message Response Times**

Messages sent through the customer portal are handled separately from emails. The Authority aims
to respond to portal messages within one working day of receipt. This faster target reflects the
expectation that customers who use the portal are seeking a quicker response.

Portal messages are triaged by the Customer Experience Team. Messages that require input from
another department, such as billing or operational services, are forwarded with a note of the
response deadline. The receiving department is responsible for ensuring that the response is sent
before the deadline.

**11.5 Written Correspondence**

Letters and other written correspondence should be acknowledged within five working days of
receipt. A full response should be provided within ten working days. Where a full response cannot
be provided within this period, the customer should be sent an interim reply explaining the reason
for the delay and providing a date by which a full response can be expected.

**11.6 Social Media**

The Authority monitors its social media accounts during contact centre hours. Queries received via
social media should be acknowledged within two hours during these hours. Where a query requires a
detailed response, the customer should be asked to provide their contact details so that a full
response can be sent by email or letter.

Social media is not intended for urgent reports, such as a loss of supply or a sewer flood.
Customers who report urgent issues via social media are asked to call the emergency line.

**11.7 Complaints Handling**

The Authority operates a two-stage complaints procedure, in line with the requirements of the
Consumer Council for Water.

Stage one: A complaint should be acknowledged within two working days of receipt. A full response
should be provided within ten working days. If the complaint is complex and a full response cannot
be provided within this period, the customer should be informed of the reason and a revised
response date should be agreed.

**12. Data Protection and Information Governance**

**12.1 Overview**

The Authority is registered with the Information Commissioner's Office under the Data Protection Act 2018 and the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR). All staff who handle personal data must comply with the data protection principles set out in Article 5 of the UK GDPR and with the Authority's internal policies on information governance.

This section sets out the standards that apply to the handling of customer data, the retention of records, and the management of information requests. It should be read alongside the Authority's Data Protection Policy (DP/01) and the Records Management Policy (RM/03).

**12.2 Definitions**

For the purposes of this manual:

- **Personal data** means any information relating to an identified or identifiable living individual.
- **Special category data** means personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health, or data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation.
- **Processing** means any operation or set of operations performed on personal data, whether by automated means or not.
- **Data subject** means the individual to whom the personal data relates.
- **Records** means all information created, received, and maintained as evidence and as an asset by the Authority, regardless of format.

**12.3 Data Protection Principles**

All processing of personal data must be carried out in accordance with the following principles:

1. Lawfulness, fairness, and transparency. Personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly, and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject.
2. Purpose limitation. Personal data must be collected for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner that is incompatible with those purposes.
3. Data minimisation. Personal data must be adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which it is processed.
4. Accuracy. Personal data must be accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date. Every reasonable step must be taken to ensure that inaccurate personal data is erased or rectified without delay.
5. Storage limitation. Personal data must be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the data is processed.
6. Integrity and confidentiality. Personal data must be processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing, accidental loss, destruction, or damage.
7. Accountability. The Authority must be able to demonstrate compliance with the principles.

**12.4 Lawful Bases for Processing**

The Authority processes personal data for a number of purposes, including the provision of water and sewerage services, billing, the handling of complaints and enquiries, and the fulfilment of its statutory duties. The lawful bases most commonly relied upon are:

- **Performance of a contract** – for example, where processing is necessary to supply water to a customer under the terms of their supply agreement.
- **Legal obligation** – for example, where processing is necessary to comply with a statutory duty, such as the reporting of water quality incidents to the Drinking Water Inspectorate.
- **Public task** – for example, where processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest, such as the management of public sewers.
- **Legitimate interests** – for example, for the prevention and detection of fraud, or for network planning and maintenance.
- **Consent** – where no other lawful basis applies, the Authority will seek the consent of the data subject. Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous.

**TVWA Service Standards Manual 2024**

**Section 13 – Performance Reporting and Improvement**

**13.1 Purpose of This Section**

This section sets out how the Authority measures, reports, and improves its performance against the service standards defined elsewhere in this Manual. It applies to all Directorates and to any contractor or agent acting on the Authority’s behalf.

**13.2 Reporting Cycle**

Performance against the standards in this Manual is reported on a quarterly basis. The reporting periods are:

- **Q1:** 1 April to 30 June
- **Q2:** 1 July to 30 September
- **Q3:** 1 October to 31 December
- **Q4:** 1 January to 31 March

The Compliance Team will publish a Quarterly Performance Report no later than twenty (20) business days after the end of each reporting period. Reports are circulated to the Executive Leadership Team, the Customer Services Committee, and, on request, to elected members of constituent councils.

An annual summary of performance is published on the Authority’s website by 30 June each year, covering the preceding calendar year.

**13.3 Key Performance Indicators**

The Authority uses the following key performance indicators (KPIs) to monitor delivery of its service standards. Each KPI is linked to the relevant section of this Manual.

| KPI | Description | Target | Manual Ref |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KPI-01 | Calls answered within 30 seconds | 85% | Section 4 |
| KPI-02 | Written enquiries acknowledged within 2 business days | 95% | Section 4 |
| KPI-03 | Written enquiries resolved within 10 business days | 90% | Section 4 |
| KPI-04 | Emergency calls attended on site within 2 hours | 98% | Section 5 |
| KPI-05 | Non-emergency jobs completed within target date | 92% | Section 5 |
| KPI-06 | Supply interruptions restored within 3 hours | 95% | Section 6 |
| KPI-07 | Complaints acknowledged within 5 business days | 100% | Section 8 |
| KPI-08 | Complaints resolved within 20 business days | 90% | Section 8 |
| KPI-09 | Billing enquiries resolved within 10 business days | 95% | Section 10 |

**13.4 Data Collection and Validation**

All performance data is recorded in the Authority’s Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system. Field staff are required to update job records on the day the work is completed, using the standard status codes set out in the Field Operations Handbook.

The Compliance Team performs a monthly data quality check on a random sample of 5% of records to verify that:

- Status codes are accurate and up to date;
- Completion dates and times are recorded correctly;
- Customer contact details are current; and
- Any notes added by staff are clear and sufficient.

Where errors are identified, the relevant Team Leader is notified and corrective action is taken. Persistent data quality issues are escalated to the Head of Customer Services.

**13.5 Customer Satisfaction Surveys**

Customer satisfaction is measured through two channels:

- **Transactional surveys** – issued by SMS or email following a completed service job, such as a repair or a visit to a customer’s property. These are sent within two business days of job completion.
- **Annual customer survey** – conducted by an independent research agency each autumn. The survey covers a representative sample of domestic and business customers and includes questions on overall satisfaction, value for money, and specific service areas.

Survey results are analysed by the Customer Insight Team and reported to the Executive Leadership Team. Action plans are developed where satisfaction scores fall below target.

**13.6 Continuous Improvement Programme**

The Authority operates a continuous improvement programme, known as **“TVWA Forward”**, to identify and implement improvements to services. The programme is overseen by the Continuous Improvement Manager and supported by a cross-directorate steering group.

The primary objectives of the project are:

1. Replace 4.2 km of cast-iron water mains with modern ductile iron and polyethylene pipework, reducing the risk of burst and leakage.
2. Reduce the frequency of unplanned supply interruptions in the project area by 60% within the first 12 months of completion.
3. Improve water quality by eliminating internal corrosion and sediment accumulation in the old mains.
4. Minimise disruption to residents and businesses through careful traffic management, phased working, and timely reinstatement.
5. Complete all works within the approved budget and programme, achieving a >95% customer satisfaction rating for post-works reinstatement.

3. Scope

In scope:

- Replacement of water mains along the following roads: Aldermere High Street (from the junction with Station Road to the junction with Mill Lane), Chapel Lane, Elm Grove, and the northern half of Priory Road.
- Installation of new service connections to all properties affected by the main replacement, up to and including the external stop tap.
- Replacement of associated hydrants, valves, and air valves.
- Temporary supply arrangements (overland supply pipes) to maintain continuity of supply to customers during the works.
- Reinstatement of highways, footways, and gardens disturbed by the works, to the satisfaction of the Borough Council and the relevant highway authority.
- Post-commissioning flushing, sampling, and disinfection of the new mains.

Out of scope:

- Replacement of private supply pipes from the external stop tap to the internal property boundary.
- Works on trunk mains or strategic distribution mains not identified above.
- Landscaping or permanent reinstatement of private gardens beyond the standard seeding and turfing specification.
